Variable merge node
The variable merge node in the workflow can integrate the output variables of multiple branch workflows into one, facilitating the unified configuration of downstream nodes.​
Description​
If multiple branches are designed in the workflow, a node is often needed to merge the output results of all branches as the final output of the workflow. If any branch is not executed, the aggregation output node will read an empty value from that branch, causing an error in the workflow operation. In this scenario, you can use a variable merge node to merge the output variables of multiple branches. The variable aggregation node will read the first non-empty value from the multiple branches for use and operation by the downstream nodes of the process, eliminating the need to handle the output results of unexecuted branches, thus simplifying the management of the data flow.​
For example, a selector or intent recognition node will split the workflow into multiple branches. Each time it is executed, the workflow will decide which branch to run based on the selector condition or user intent, at which point the output variables of the other unexecuted branches are empty. You can connect all the branches to the variable merge node and set an output variable. Regardless of which branch is executed, its result can be referenced and accessed through this variable, avoiding the repeated definition of output variables with the same semantics in downstream nodes.​
The variable merge node supports grouped aggregation, where each group of variables will be merged into one output variable, and the data types within the group must be the same.​
Configure variable merge node​
When configuring the variable merge node, you need to select the merge strategy and merge variables, and set the merge group as needed.​
Merge strategy​
The merging process for all variables in each group is done by specifying a strategy, with variables within the same group implementing the corresponding merge strategy.​
Currently, the merge strategy only supports the setting "return the first non-empty value in each group." You can drag variables and adjust their positions. For example, set three variables output1, output2, and output3 sequentially within a group to be merged into one variable Group1. If output1 is not empty, assign the value of output1 to Group1; if output1 is empty, take the value of output2, and so on.​
​
​
​
​
​
Merge variables​
In Group 1, select the variables you need to merge. The data types of variables within a group must be the same.​
The variable merge node supports merging various data types, including strings (String), numbers (Integer, Number), files (File), objects (Object), and arrays (Array), etc.​
Each group can only merge variables of one data type. For example, you can merge multiple string type variables into one string variable, or merge multiple integer type variables into one integer variable.​
Merge group​
By default, there is only one group, Group1, corresponding to one output variable, Group1. All variable types in Group1 are the same as the variable type of output. If you need to output multiple variables, you can add multiple groups. For example, if each branch has two output variables, String and Integer, you can set up two groups to merge String and Integer respectively.​
​
​
​
​
​
Output​
The output variable of the variable merge node is fixed as Group1, which is the result of the merge of Group1. The specific value depends on the merge strategy. If there are multiple groups, they are incremented according to the number of groups to be Group2, Group3, and so on. The data type of the output variable depends on the data type of the variables merged in the corresponding group.​
Example​
In home tutoring AI apps, the IF condition is used to determine which subject category the user's input question belongs to, and the corresponding question is routed to the appropriate branch for processing. For instance, a math question is routed to a math branch's large model for a response. The three branches are all merged into a variable merge node, summarized into two parameters: subject type (type) and answer (answer), which are then passed to the end node to answer the user's question.​
The overall process is as follows:​
​
​
​
​
​
The node configuration is as follows:​
​
Node type​
	
Description​
	
Example​


Start node​
	
Define two variables:​
BOT_USER_INPUT: The question input by the user, which is the student's question.​
type: The subject corresponding to the question.​
	
​
​
​
​
​


Condition node​
	
Judge which subject the user's input type belongs to and route the question to the corresponding branch for processing. Here we define two branches for Chinese and Mathematics, and all other subjects are routed to another branch.​
​
	
​
​
​
​
​


LLM node​
	
Used to answer questions related to the corresponding subject. You need to be set:​
Input: Define the query variable, referencing the user's question collected by the start node.​
System prompt: Set up the persona for the subject teacher, which can be generated automatically by AI.​
User prompt: Set as {{query}}, directly referencing the query variable.​
Output: Define two variables:​
answer: Answer generated by the model.​
type: Subject type. For example, the fixed value for Chinese language node is "Chinese".​
	
​
​
​
​
​
​


Variable merge node​
	
Merge the two output variables answer and type from the LLM node. Each group can only merge one variable, so we need to set two groups.​
